finding.claim: GET /mirror fetches an attacker-supplied URL. The only host check is a bare suffix test (host.endswith('example.com')) with no dot boundary, so hosts such as evilexample.com pass. An attacker who controls DNS for such a domain can point it at internal or metadata addresses. The response leaks only len(r.text).
finding.source: mirror.py:11 - url: str query parameter of GET /mirror

trace.note: Attacker-controlled url query parameter enters the handler
host = urlparse(url).hostname or '' extracts the hostname
if not host.endswith('example.com'): suffix match with no leading dot, so evilexample.com and xexample.com pass
Only the suffix test gates the request; no scheme, port, IP-literal, or resolved-address checks follow
The same raw, unvalidated url string is passed to httpx, which connects to the named host after DNS resolution with no IP-range filtering
Only len(r.text) is returned, a weak oracle

finding.guards_checked: (1) Host check at mirror.py:12-14: suffix-only, no dot boundary, so any attacker-registrable domain ending in 'example.com' bypasses it. (2) Scheme: not checked, but httpx only fetches http/https, so file:// is not reachable. (3) Redirects: httpx.AsyncClient defaults to follow_redirects=False, so redirects cannot escape the check. (4) Resolved-IP, private-range, and metadata blocking: none; the check is on the name, not the connected address. (5) Parser differential between urlparse (validation) and httpx (fetch): not tested, so not claimed.

verdict.guard_found: None closing. mirror.py:13 is `host.endswith("example.com")`, a suffix test with no leading dot, so evilexample.com passes; it is the only check. No middleware or other files exist (Glob returned only mirror.py), and mirror.py:16 `c.get(url)` has no resolved-IP or private-range filtering.
verdict.reason: The unauthenticated `url` query parameter (mirror.py:11) reaches `c.get(url)` at mirror.py:16 behind only the bypassable suffix check at mirror.py:13, so an attacker can register evilexample.com, point it at internal or metadata IPs, and receive len(r.text) back via mirror.py:17.
